memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: routine follow‑up of polycystic ovary syndrome, coronary artery disease and insomnia.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She reports stable exertional dyspnoea on walking 200 m, occasional palpitations, and difficulty falling asleep despite melatonin.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/82 mmHg, pulse 78/min regular, weight 55 kg, height 150 cm, BMI 24.4 (overweight). No peripheral edema, lungs clear, cardiac rhythm regular sinus, no murmurs.
IMPRESSION: 1. PCOS – on metformin and OC pill, HbA1c 5.8% (pre‑diabetic range), testosterone mildly elevated. 2. CAD – on aspirin, atorvastatin, metoprolol, isosorbide mononitrate, GTN SOS; lipid profile shows LDL 110 mg/dL. 3. Insomnia – melatonin 3 mg HS, reports nocturnal awakenings.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current medicines. Advise diet low in refined carbs, increase walking to 30 min daily. Return if chest pain, breathlessness > usual, fever >39°C, or bloody stools. Influenza vaccine not due today (outside autumn).

memories.author: D03
memories.text: ECG: Sinus rhythm, rate 76/min. No ST‑segment depression or elevation. QRS duration 92 ms. Left ventricular voltage within normal limits. No pathologic Q waves. Impression: Normal ECG for age.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been waking up around 3 am most nights and find it hard to get back to sleep. I feel a bit more tired during the day and noticed my heart racing when I climb the auto‑rickshaw seat.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: review of insomnia symptoms and lipid results.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports worsening sleep onset latency, frequent nocturnal awakenings, and occasional daytime palpitations.
EXAMINATION: BP 142/86 mmHg, pulse 80/min, weight 55 kg, BMI 24.4 (overweight). No new cardiac murmurs, lungs clear.
IMPRESSION: 1. Insomnia – persistent despite melatonin; consider adding low‑dose trazodone. 2. CAD – LDL remains above target; consider intensifying statin. 3. PCOS – HbA1c stable.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase atorvastatin to 40 mg HS (already) – actually continue; add trazodone 50 mg HS for sleep. Advise weight‑neutral diet, limit caffeine after 4 pm, regular bedtime routine. Return if chest pain, palpitations with dizziness, breathlessness at rest, or fever >39°C. Influenza vaccine not due.

memories.text: Transthoracic echocardiogram: Left ventricular ejection fraction 58% (normal). Mild left atrial enlargement. No significant valvular stenosis or regurgitation. No regional wall motion abnormality. Impression: Normal systolic function, no evidence of ischemic cardiomyopathy.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: annual review and influenza vaccination.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports improved sleep on trazodone, occasional mild palpitations on exertion, otherwise well.
EXAMINATION: BP 140/84 mmHg, pulse 78/min, weight 55 kg, BMI 24.4 (overweight). Lungs clear, cardiac rhythm regular.
IMPRESSION: 1. PCOS – stable on metformin and OC pill, HbA1c 5.7%. 2. CAD – LDL 102 mg/dL, continue atorvastatin, aspirin, metoprolol, isosorbide mononitrate. 3. Insomnia – trazodone 50 mg HS effective, melatonin continued.
ARRANGEMENTS: Influenza vaccine administered today (2026-04-08). Advise continue low‑salt diet, maintain walking 30 min daily, limit alcohol. Return if chest pain, breathlessness at rest, fever >39°C, or sudden swelling of legs. Next review in 6 months.
